summary: Throughput plateau on dedicated cluster caused by sudden KV-cache bloom and autoscaler misclassification
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer (Arcadia Health) observed a persistent throughput plateau on their dedicated pool between 09:40–11:20 UTC. Token rates p50/p95 stopped improving despite steady incoming QPS; p99 rose slightly. No clear GPU allocation failures reported.

Impact:
- Arcadia's inference latency degraded and batch queues grew for short/medium-length streaming requests. Business impact: user-facing feature degraded for ~1.5 hours.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity in prod (us-east), reserved cluster id: rc-87b2. Affected routes are primarily short-stream streaming endpoints pinned to redwood/gptx-13b-v1.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Replay ~10k short streaming requests (avg 120 tokens) routed to the dedicated pool with KV caching enabled.
2) Observe slot utilization and autoscaler reactions over a 30–60 minute sustained window.

Observed metrics and logs:
- KV cache size (entries) increased 4x in a 20m window (dashboard link below).
- Batch formation rate decreased, average batch sizes dropped from 16->6, CPU prefetch jobs spiked.
- Autoscaler saw increased ephemeral CPU and classified nodes as "underutilized" at the wrong time, triggering conservative retention and preventing additional slot warmups.
- No 5xx spike; 504s limited to a handful of long-lived streams.
- Relevant dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/boards/dedicated/rc-87b2-cache-bloom

Immediate ask:
- Temporary mitigation to restore throughput while we investigate root cause and whether this is a noisy-neighbor or internal KV-cache behavior.

2026-03-10 10:22 - SRE (Lucas Chen): Pulled cluster logs and autoscaler decision traces. Noted a spike in cache insert rate at 09:42 UTC. Sharing traces: https://logs.redwood/trace/87b2/ins-4492
2026-03-10 10:48 - Arcadia (customer): We replayed a subset of traffic and saw p50 latency stabilize only after disabling KV caching on the route. Re-enabled later and issue returned.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Workaround applied: disabled KV cache for affected route and requested temporary slot retention bump from infra (30m). Asking infra to hold autoscaler from shrinking for 15m.

2026-03-11 09:15 - Eng (Priya Rao): Investigating whether prefetch workers are holding CPU locks long enough to block batch formation under high cache churn. Running synthetic reproducer against staging.

2026-03-12 08:40 - SRE (Lucas Chen): Replicating in staging with a traffic pattern that produces a KV-cache bloom; confirmed autoscaler heuristics misinterpreted CPU bursts as low utilization. Preparing candidate fix to ignore ephemeral prefetch CPU spikes.
2026-03-12 12:01 - Support (Maya Patel): Notified Arcadia of planned follow-ups and temporary safeguards.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: (1) KV-cache bloom — large number of new prefixes pushed cache growth, causing prefetch/eviction churn that reduces batching efficiency; (2) Autoscaler misclassification — autoscaler uses short-window CPU metrics and saw spike then rapid fall, interpreted as low sustained load and trimmed slots; (3) Noisy neighbor — another tenant caused intermittent small-stream fanout increasing cache churn.

What we checked:
- Cache insert/delete rates and median TTLs. Found burst of new cache entries starting 09:42 UTC from route /v1/streaming/generate (Arcadia).
- CPU and GPU metrics annotated with trace ids. Observed prefetch CPU spikes tightly coupled with cache insert rate.
- Autoscaler decision logs show shrink actions at 09:58 and 10:04 that reduced reserved slots by 2 despite incoming queue depth still > threshold.
- Cross-tenant telemetry: no other tenant had matching traffic pattern in the same pool during the window. Noise is likely internal to Arcadia workload.

Reproducer in staging:
- Synthetic traffic that creates many distinct prefixes per user session reproduces batch collapse and autoscaler shrink within 20–40 minutes.

Temporary experiments run:
- Disabling KV cache on route restored batch sizes and throughput.
- Holding autoscaler (prevent shrink) during reproducer keeps throughput stable but is not a long-term fix.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied (2026-03-10): Disabled KV caching on the affected route and asked infra to disable autoscaler shrink for rc-87b2 for 30m. Throughput returned to expected levels.

Short-term fix (in progress): We will patch autoscaler to 1) ignore sub-1m CPU spikes from prefetch workers when making shrink decisions and 2) add a short hysteresis window tied to batch formation drop metrics. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7123 (testing in staging).

Long-term actions (post-incident tasks):
- Add improved telemetry for KV-cache churn (per-route insert rate & eviction backpressure) and link to autoscaler heuristics.
- Update runbook: when cache bloom is detected, temporarily throttle prefetchers and prefer slot retention until batch sizes recover. (Confluence: Cache Bloom Runbook).
- Customer follow-up: advise Arcadia on request routing and prefix cardinality; provide recommended caching knobs for their workload.

Follow-ups created: INT-23121 (autoscaler metrics instrumentation), SUP-954010 (Arcadia config advisory), and OPS task to add rapid rollback playbook.
final_notes: Incident still open while autoscaler patch is validated in staging. Customer workaround stable; Arcadia reported business impact was limited after mitigation. Next update planned after staging validation (2026-03-13).
